decisions.decision: Take route (b): remove provider.Invocation.Environment, and with it Grant.Apply and ProviderClient.Grant, rather than making SupervisedInvocationRunner.Run read the declared field. The outcome permits either route and names the judging criterion; the criterion is which route narrows the authority over the environment that reaches the child, and (b) wins that comparison outright.
decisions.rationale: Measured at 47b53c9, the child's environment is already an exclusive, total description sourced from one place. internal/runner/supervisor.go:88 assigns cmd.Env = s.Env, which REPLACES the parent environment rather than adding to it, and SupervisedInvocationRunner.Run always sets sup.Env (internal/runner/provider.go:462) from buildEnvironmentFromBaseNames(record.EnvironmentBaseNames) (:435), which fails closed if any declared base name is unset (:270-280) and is then checked by GuardEnvironment against an allowlist derived from that same record (:448). So today the digest-bound approved provider-preflight record is not merely the primary authority over the child's environment, it is the complete and only one, and the totality is enforced by a replacement assignment rather than by convention. Route (a) would take a set that is currently total and merge a second contributor into it. Route (b) keeps the totality and makes it structurally unavoidable: with the field deleted there is no place for a second contributor to travel, so the property stops being a runtime fact about what Run happens to read and becomes a property of the type system. That is strictly the narrower authority, and it is the same reasoning V2-017 d8 used to prove credential isolation as an absence rather than as a check.

decisions.decision: Reject route (a) explicitly, with its strongest form stated so nobody re-proposes a weaker one. The strongest (a) is not a blind merge: it is Run merging inv.Environment onto the base environment while refusing fail-closed unless every NAME carried by the invocation is already named in the approved record's environment.granted_names, and unless every NAME the two share carries an identical value. Even that form is rejected.
decisions.rationale: Three measured reasons. First, its guard cannot be exercised against any record that exists: all three records in .agents/v2/provider-preflight/ declare granted_names as the empty array, and internal/contracts/provider_preflight.go rule 4 forbids a non-empty granted_names whenever provider.name is claude, which is the only provider any record names. The intersection between what (a) would deliver and what any approved record authorises is provably empty, so (a) ships an unexercised merge inside the one function that hands an environment to a real child process. Second, (a) concedes two authorities and then detects their disagreement. Fail-closed on disagreement is the minimum bar, not the goal: a design that must compare two sources is weaker than one that has a single source, because the comparison is code that can be wrong while the absence of a field cannot. Third, (a) demotes V2-017 d8(c) from a structural claim to a conditional one. Today 'the child's environment is exactly the approved record's base names' is provable by reading one call site; after (a) it holds only when the invocation happens to carry nothing, which is precisely the shape of assumption that made this defect latent for three live exercises.

decisions.decision: Deleting the field is not sufficient on its own, because deletion alone would convert a silently-dropped grant into a silently-ignored declaration. Add one fail-closed refusal to SupervisedInvocationRunner.Run: after LoadPreflightRecord and strictly before Ledger.Reserve, refuse with a new sentinel when len(record.EnvironmentGranted) != 0. No process is started, no reservation is debited, nothing is repaired and nothing is delivered.
decisions.rationale: environment.granted_names is measured to be loaded (internal/runner/costledger.go:143) and read by nothing except a live assertion that it is empty (internal/runner/provider_live_test.go:530). It is therefore the same defect shape one level up: an approved, digest-bound declaration that the execution path does not honour. It must NOT be deleted like Invocation.Environment, because unlike that field it is schema-required (contracts/schemas/provider-preflight.json), it is semantically enforced (rule 4 forbids it for claude), and it is bound by an approval digest, so removing it would delete real enforcement and require a contracts change. The correct closure is the opposite of deletion: honour it by refusing. This is what makes 'rebuilding from the record is the stronger guarantee' a proof rather than an assertion -- the record is stronger precisely because it is the one place where a declaration the runner cannot deliver is visible and can be refused before any cost is incurred. The position before Reserve is load-bearing for the reason V2-077 established: a reservation debited before a refusal stays charged at worst case forever (dp-v2-017 d9).

decisions.decision: Where the value Grant.Apply wrote actually went: nowhere that ever started a process. Grant.Apply (internal/runner/secret_broker.go:92-98) is the ONLY writer of Invocation.Environment in the whole tree -- the adapters' single shared build helper constructs Invocation{Argv, Stdin, WorkingDirectory} and never sets it (internal/provider/adapters.go:47). Its only caller is ProviderClient.Run under `if c.Grant != nil` (internal/runner/provider.go:532-534), and ProviderClient.Grant is set by no file, test or otherwise: the only two construction sites are internal/runner/journey_test.go:159 and internal/runner/crash_test.go:165/205/284/319, none of which set it. The value therefore reached exactly one destination in the entire history of the field: the []provider.Invocation slice inside FakeInvocationRunner, where a test read it back.
decisions.rationale: This is the difference between a field that is dangerous and a field that is decorative. A field written by one function, whose one caller is never given the input that triggers it, and whose one reader records values for assertions, has never carried a byte toward a process. Stating the destination precisely is what licenses deletion rather than repair: there is no in-flight behaviour to preserve, no caller to migrate and no production path to keep working.

decisions.decision: What FakeInvocationRunner was observing was the Grant's own leased channel, not the Invocation's field. The field was the vehicle the A11 test happened to inspect it through. Retarget the positive control of TestSecretBrokerCredentialNeverLeaksExceptIntoOneInvocationEnvironment from runner.Calls[0].Environment to grant.Environment(), and change nothing else in that test.
decisions.rationale: That test's actual claim is an absence over six durable or observable surfaces -- the journal file, the marshalled Work Packet, the bounded log file, the canonical store's EventsPage, the marshalled AcceptResultResponse, and every element of os.Args and Invocation.Argv -- and a positive control that keeps the absence from being vacuous. Every absence target is downstream of the Work Packet and the argv, not of the environment, so none of them changes. The positive control's only job is to prove the crypto/rand fixture the test generated is genuinely the value the broker produced, so that the absence scans are over the right bytes; grant.Environment() proves exactly that, at exactly the same strength, one hop earlier. If retargeting the control cost the test any strength, that would itself have been evidence that the field carried something -- it does not, which is the measurement.

decisions.decision: Keep SecretBroker, Scope, Grant, Grant.Environment() and Lease with all five fail-closed refusals. Delete only the delivery channel that pretended to work: Grant.Apply and ProviderClient.Grant. Correct Grant.Environment()'s doc comment, which currently promises 'the code path that is about to merge it into a child process environment', to state that no such path exists today and to name the one shape a future path may take.
decisions.rationale: The broker is the authorisation mechanism -- Permit under effective stop, a non-zero and matching fencing token, a per-provider name allowlist, single use, revocation -- and every one of those refusals has its own test. None of them depends on the deleted field. Deleting the broker would be far outside the outcome and would remove the only place in the design where a credential has a legitimate home. The distinction that decides what goes and what stays: Invocation.Environment sits on the type whose entire purpose is 'the description of the child process to start', so a reader is entitled to conclude the child receives it -- that is the lie. Grant.Environment() is an accessor on a leased grant and claims nothing about any child; once its doc stops claiming one, it pretends nothing.

decisions.decision: The sanctioned future shape, recorded here so a later task does not reinvent the deleted field: when a grant must genuinely reach a child, SupervisedInvocationRunner leases exactly the names the approved record's environment.granted_names declares and merges the leased values into the environment it already builds -- names from the record, values from the broker, never a name that the record did not authorise. The d3 refusal is then replaced by that delivery, in a task with its own credential-isolation acceptance. Do not re-add a field on provider.Invocation to do it.
decisions.rationale: That shape keeps the authority count at one: the digest-bound record remains the sole authority over WHICH names reach the child, and the broker supplies only values, which a record can never carry because a record is committed text. It is also the shape that makes the d3 refusal a milestone rather than a wall: the refusal exists exactly because the delivery does not, and whoever builds the delivery deletes the refusal in the same change. Naming it now is what prevents the next author from restoring an Invocation field because it looked like the obvious seam.

decisions.decision: V2-077's landed guard test is neither deleted nor merely inverted: it is generalised into the guard that closes the whole class. TestInvocationEnvironmentStaysUnconsumedByTheRunner keeps its exact name and gains four assertions: (1) by reflection, provider.Invocation's exported field set is exactly {Argv, Stdin, WorkingDirectory}; (2) by the existing AST scan of SupervisedInvocationRunner.Run, every field in that set is read by Run, and Run reads no selector on inv outside that set; (3) Environment specifically is absent from the set, with a failure message that carries dp-v2-078 d7's instruction; (4) by reflection, Grant has no method named Apply and ProviderClient has no field named Grant. V2-077's original measurement and its date stay in the comment as history rather than being deleted, and the comment records that V2-078 chose route (b) and why.
decisions.rationale: V2-077's test asserted the ABSENCE of a read. Under (b) that assertion becomes unfalsifiable, because a read of a field that does not exist cannot compile -- a guard that cannot fail is not a guard. Assertion (2) is what replaces it with something that can fail, and it is stronger than either V2-077's or a naive (b) inversion: V2-077's defect and V2-078's defect are the same shape, 'the Invocation declares something the runner does not consume', and (1)+(2) together make that class mechanically checked instead of enumerating its two known instances. Adding a field to provider.Invocation without consuming it in Run now turns the test red at once, which is exactly the notification neither V2-077 nor V2-078 received. Assertion (4) pins the deletions themselves so a revert is loud. The name must not change for a reason beyond continuity: nothing else would tell a future reader that this file is where the recorded defect became a removal.

decisions.decision: The name TestSecretBrokerCredentialNeverLeaksExceptIntoOneInvocationEnvironment does not change either, and the test's comment states that 'one invocation environment' now names the one leased Grant environment destined for one invocation -- the channel, not a struct field.
decisions.rationale: This is a hard constraint, not a preference: internal/reconciler/failure_matrix_test.go:77 carries that test's name as a string literal, as the linked test for the 'secret-like fixture in commit, log, Provider outbound' row of docs/architecture/failure-model.md section 10. internal/reconciler/** is prohibited in this task, so a rename would either silently stale that row or force an edit outside the allowed set. Rewording the comment costs nothing and keeps the failure matrix honest.

decisions.decision: This task closes a latent defect, not an open hole, and the Work Order must say so in those words. Measured: no non-test file anywhere constructs a SecretBroker (the only constructors are internal/runner/secret_broker_test.go and internal/runner/provider_live_test.go:538); no file at all sets ProviderClient.Grant; all three records in .agents/v2/provider-preflight/ declare granted_names as []; contracts rule 4 forbids a non-empty granted_names for claude, the only provider with a record; and cmd/runner/main.go carries no provider wiring at all -- it refuses to start without --fake and prints 'no external control-plane wiring is enabled'. There is therefore no production path today by which a non-empty grant can exist, and no credential has ever been dropped.
decisions.rationale: Conflating a latent defect with an active one corrupts both the evidence and the next reader's risk judgement. What this task actually buys is that the day someone grants something, the system refuses loudly (d3) instead of running with a silently narrower environment, and that the misleading seam that would have absorbed the grant is gone (d1). Saying that plainly is also what keeps the task honest about its own size: it passes no release gate and satisfies no M6 completion condition.

decisions.decision: Two further contributors to the child's environment are recorded as measured facts and deliberately NOT changed. (a) SupervisedInvocationRunner.ExtraEnv (internal/runner/provider.go:246-254) is the one additive source outside the record; it is set in exactly one place in the tree, internal/runner/provider_live_test.go:1004, for dp-v2-017 B16/I7's deliberate transport-failure diagnostic, and it extends the GuardEnvironment allowlist for its own names (:440-447). (b) Grant.id (internal/runner/secret_broker.go:221) is written and read by nothing.
decisions.rationale: The single-authority claim must be stated with its one declared exception rather than overstated, or the evidence is wrong in the same way the comments this task corrects are wrong: ExtraEnv means the honest claim is 'exactly the approved record's base names, plus one declared diagnostic override that is guarded by the same allowlist mechanism and used by one live invocation'. ExtraEnv is not the defect this task removes -- it is read by the production path, it is documented, and it is guarded -- so removing it would be a different task's judgement. Grant.id is the same 'field nothing reads' shape as the field being deleted and therefore tempting to ride along, but it is unexported, so it cannot mislead any caller, and a per-grant identity is what a revocation or audit record would need; deleting it in this change would also blur which deletion d8's guard is guarding. Record both, act on neither -- which is the discipline V2-077 exercised on this very task.

decisions.decision: Every comment and document that argues from the deleted field is corrected in the same change, and each correction keeps the historical measurement with its date rather than erasing it. The six sites, re-measured by the implementer rather than copied: internal/runner/provider.go:84-93 (FakeInvocationRunner's doc), internal/runner/secret_broker.go:17-24 and :78-88 (the two-channel header and Grant's doc), internal/runner/supervisor.go:15-17 (which calls Env 'the only place a Secret Broker grant may be merged into a child's environment'), internal/provider/pool.go:22-25 (which calls Grant.Apply 'the only path that merges a value into an Invocation environment'), internal/provider/adapters_test.go:141-145, and docs/operations/runner-local.md:409-416.
decisions.rationale: A comment naming a channel that no longer exists is the same defect as a field that pretends to be delivered: it is a claim the code does not honour, and it is how the next author concludes that a credential path exists. supervisor.go and pool.go both assert a uniqueness ('the only place', 'the only path') that becomes false the moment Apply is gone, so leaving either would actively mislead. Keeping each historical measurement with its date is V2-077 A8's own convention and is what lets a reader see that the conclusion was reached from a measurement rather than assumed.

decisions.decision: No live Provider invocation is required by this task, and none is authorised by it. Record the G6b consequence instead: this diff touches internal/provider/provider.go and internal/runner/provider.go, which are inside the file set the live exercise compiles, so it does invalidate the diff-intersection freshness of the existing provider-live records for any FUTURE gate that needs them. That cost is recorded and escalated to the coordinator, not paid here.
decisions.rationale: V2-077's outcome was about what a real child actually does with a real directory, so re-observation was the only way to see it; this outcome is that a field is gone and that a declaration is refused, and neither is observable to a child. The environment a real claude child receives is byte-identical before and after: it is built by the same call to buildEnvironmentFromBaseNames from the same record. Spending a live invocation to observe an unchanged environment would consume a single-holder subscription resource to re-confirm a property the type system now enforces. The measured state also argues against bundling one: V2-075's ledger stands at 12 of 12 with halted false, V2-077's own re-observation was never run (ev-v2-077-runner is result 'partial' with a10 recorded skipped) and no V2-077 preflight record exists, so a live run here would need a NEW owner-approved record -- an owner act this task must never fabricate.

verification: devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/runner ./internal/provider, green, with the deletions in place and every pre-existing top-level test name still present and passing.

devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -run TestInvocationEnvironmentStaysUnconsumedByTheRunner -v ./internal/runner, green, with the four d8 assertions present; and the same test asserted to FAIL when a scratch field is temporarily added to provider.Invocation and not consumed by Run, so the class guard is proven able to fail rather than assumed able.

devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -run TestSecretBrokerCredentialNeverLeaksExceptIntoOneInvocationEnvironment -v ./internal/runner, green under its unchanged name, with the positive control retargeted to grant.Environment() and every absence target unchanged; plus a temporary negative control in which the positive control is fed an unrelated random value and the test is observed to fail, proving the control is not vacuous.

devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -run 'TestSupervisedInvocationRunner|TestCostLedger' -v ./internal/runner, green, including the new d3 case: a fixture record with provider.name codex and a non-empty environment.granted_names makes Run return the new sentinel, with no ledger file created and no process started.

devbox run --pure -- make component-runner and devbox run --pure -- make component-provider and devbox run --pure -- make component-docs, each judged by its own verdict line rather than by the shell exit status.
devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts, green with the two evidence records registered in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json.
devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/reconciler, green, proving the failure-matrix row that names the A11 test by string literal still resolves.

git grep -n 'Invocation.Environment' over the final tree returns only historical comment text that carries its own date, and git grep -n '\.Environment' over non-test Go files returns no selector on an Invocation-typed value.
devbox run --pure -- gitleaks dir .agents --config .gitleaks.toml, run after the evidence commit, clean.
risks: The d3 refusal is a behaviour change on a path no record currently exercises. If a future record legitimately declares granted_names before the d7 delivery exists, the runner will refuse it. That is intended and is the point of the refusal, but it must be documented in docs/operations/runner-local.md so an operator who hits it reads a refusal rather than diagnosing a hang.

d8's reflection-based field-set assertion will fail for a future field that is legitimately consumed somewhere other than Run. The failure message must therefore instruct the reader to either consume it in Run or update the record deliberately, never to delete the test -- the same instruction V2-077 wrote and this task honours.

Deleting Grant.Apply leaves SecretBroker with no consumer in any non-test file. A later reader may read that as dead code and delete the broker. d6's corrected doc comment and d7's recorded future shape are the mitigation; if a task ever proposes deleting the broker, it must first answer where a credential would then live.

The G6b freshness of the provider-live records is invalidated by this diff (d13) without being restored. If the coordinator later needs those records fresh for a gate, the cost surfaces then rather than now. Escalate it as a coordinator-owned item at integration.

Route (b) forecloses nothing but does move the work: whoever needs a credential in a child must now build the d7 delivery deliberately, which is more work than filling a field that already existed. That is the intended trade -- the field's cheapness was exactly why nobody noticed it delivered nothing.
